title: Ext groups of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], which has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules. The functor $\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-):\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and the *Ext groups* are its right derived functors evaluated at $\mathcal G$:

$$
\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)
:=R^i\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-)(\mathcal G)
=H^i\bigl(\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet)\bigr)\qquad(i\ge0),
$$

where $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution of $\mathcal G$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $\mathcal I^n=0$ for $n<0$, and $\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ is the complex of abelian groups with differential $f\mapsto d^n\circ f$. A morphism $\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ acts through a lift to the resolutions, a morphism $a:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$ by precomposition $f\mapsto f\circ a$. These groups are independent of the resolution up to canonical isomorphism, and canonically isomorphic to the Ext groups $\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\Mod(\mathcal O_X)}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=\Hom_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(\mathcal F[0],\mathcal G[0][i])$ of the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-ext]; $\operatorname{Ext}^0_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$; a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal G''\to0$ gives a long exact sequence $0\to\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G')\to\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G'')\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G')\to\cdots\to\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G'')\to\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G')\to\cdots$; and a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ gives a long exact sequence $0\to\Hom(\mathcal F'',\mathcal G)\to\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom(\mathcal F',\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal F'',\mathcal G)\to\cdots\to\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F',\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_X(\mathcal F'',\mathcal G)\to\cdots$.

(Correction of the blueprint text, which defined $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ as $R^i\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(-,\mathcal G)(\mathcal F)$, the right derived functors of the contravariant functor $\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(-,\mathcal G)$: those would need projective resolutions in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, which does not have enough projectives, so that definition is ill-posed. The definition above is the classical one by injective resolutions of the second variable, which agrees with Stacks Derived Categories, Definition 06XQ by Lemma 06XR (1).)

proof.text: *Injective resolutions exist.* $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives] (Stacks 01DH). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1) gives every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ an injective resolution $\varepsilon:\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $\mathcal I^n=0$ for $n<0$, so the complex $\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ of the definition exists.

source.place: Section 01DH (sheaves of modules on a ringed space have enough injectives); derived.tex Definition 013I

proof.text: *$\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-)$ is additive and left exact.* It is additive since composition in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is bilinear. For a morphism $g:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ with kernel $k:\mathcal K\to\mathcal B$, the universal property of the kernel says that $f\mapsto k\circ f$ is a bijection from $\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal K)$ onto $\{f:\mathcal F\to\mathcal B\mid g\circ f=0\}=\ker\Hom(\mathcal F,g)$; so $\Hom(\mathcal F,-)$ preserves kernels. Thus it is left exact in the sense of [def-sp-left-exact-additive], whose right derived functors $R^i\Hom(\mathcal F,-)(\mathcal G)=H^i(\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ are the groups of the definition.

*Independence of the resolution, comparison with [def-pc-ext], and $\operatorname{Ext}^0=\Hom$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] with $\mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, $M=\mathcal F$, $N=\mathcal G$: for each injective resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ it gives an isomorphism $\phi_{\mathcal I}:\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\Mod(\mathcal O_X)}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet))$, sending the class of a cocycle $f$ to $\varepsilon[i]^{-1}\circ f$. For two resolutions $\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet$, $\phi_{\mathcal J}\circ\phi_{\mathcal I}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism between the two candidate groups, and these isomorphisms compose (the source group of [def-pc-ext] does not involve a resolution), so the groups are well defined up to canonical isomorphism and canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\Mod(\mathcal O_X)}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ (Stacks 06XR (1)). In degree $0$, [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2) for $v=\Hom(\mathcal F,-)$ (left exact by step 2) gives $\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet))$, $f\mapsto\varepsilon\circ f$ (Stacks 06XS (2)).

*Long exact sequence in the second variable.* $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives (step 1) and $v=\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-):\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is left exact additive (step 2). [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] applied to $v$ and $0\to\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal G''\to0$ gives connecting maps $\delta^i:\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G'')\to\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G')$ and the exactness of the stated sequence, its degree-$0$ terms being $\Hom$ by step 3.

source.place: Section 06XP, the first long exact sequence after Definition 06XQ

proof.text: *Long exact sequence in the first variable.* Let $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal F''\to0$ be exact and fix one injective resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$. For each $n$, $0\to\Hom(\mathcal F'',\mathcal I^n)\xrightarrow{p^*}\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^n)\xrightarrow{u^*}\Hom(\mathcal F',\mathcal I^n)\to0$ is exact: $p^*$ is injective because $p$ is an epimorphism; $\ker u^*=\operatorname{im}p^*$ because $p$ is a cokernel of $u$ (a map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^n$ killing $\mathcal F'$ factors uniquely through $\mathcal F''$); $u^*$ is surjective because $u$ is a monomorphism and $\mathcal I^n$ is injective, which is the definition of injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Pre- and postcomposition commute, so $p^*,u^*$ are morphisms of complexes and $0\to\Hom(\mathcal F'',\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Hom(\mathcal F',\mathcal I^\bullet)\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of abelian groups. [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] gives its long exact cohomology sequence; the complexes vanish in negative degrees, so the sequence starts with $0\to H^0$, and $H^0=\Hom$ by step 3. This is the stated sequence, the same resolution computing all three terms.
